title: You Think Consciousness Multitasks, Yet Your Brain Broadcasts Only One Thought at a Time

acts.name: 86-Billion-Neuron Supercomputer vs Single-Voice Conscious Bottleneck (1988)
sentences: You think your conscious mind runs your whole brain!
Yet one short text makes a podcast vanish!
This is the true story of Bernard Baars's Global Workspace.
Here is what went wrong with multitasking myths.
Your brain packs eighty-six billion neurons, like a city!
In the dark, hidden circuits keep your balance.
They parse grammar and steady your heart silently.
In nineteen eighty-eight, Bernard Baars asked a bold question.
Why hold just one thought — and that wasn't the strangest part.

acts.name: Binocular Rivalry Stereoscope: House vs Face Winner-Take-All Flip
sentences: In San Diego, Baars tested two open eyes!
Inside that tabletop scope, your left eye sees a house.
At that same moment, your right eye sees a face!
Both hit the visual cortex, your vision center, nonstop.
Do you see a house mixed with a face?
Or does one picture lock out the other?
Every three seconds your view flips like a slow breath!
Viewers flip one hundred percent, like a radio snapping stations!
Thinking consciousness does all brain work was a total nightmare.

acts.name: AI Shared-Board Architecture & Frontoparietal Global Broadcast
sentences: Why squeeze a vast brain through one narrow gate?
Baars borrowed a smart clue from early AI teams.
Six silent experts shared one board to solve puzzles.
Instead of doing every job, awareness works like a loudspeaker!
One winning clue steps onto a bright theater stage.
The prefrontal cortex, the planner behind your forehead, broadcasts it!
The parietal cortex, your attention spotlight, holds that scene!
Silent memory, speech, and movement rooms all listen in.
But here's the twist: who sits inside watching?

acts.name: No Inner Spectator & Tip-of-the-Tongue Broadcast Search
sentences: Critics joked that a tiny person watched a screen.
Baars proved zero little viewer sits inside your skull!
Your silent specialist networks are the audience in the dark!
Ever blanked on an actor's name at dinner?
Your stage posts one wanted notice to the room.
You chat about dessert while memory workers search.
Five minutes later, like a kettle boiling, it pops up!
Could one lonely circuit find that name alone?
Only a wide broadcast wakes the right hidden expert.

acts.name: From 2005 Cortical Broadcast Model to 2025 Nature Test on 256 Volunteers
sentences: Later on, his team mapped this stage onto brain wiring.
Brain scientists traced long bridges linking the front and back.
Would brain scans back up Baars's stage model?
In twenty twenty-five, rival labs ran a Nature test.
They scanned two hundred fifty-six volunteers, like a lecture hall!
When a picture entered awareness, wide networks lit up!
The researchers were left completely stunned.
Labs still debate timing, yet global broadcast stood firm.

acts.name: Why Verbal Multitasking Fails & How to Use Your Conscious Stage
sentences: What does Baars's theater mean for your day?
Typing an email during a podcast makes two voices clash.
Two minutes vanish, like an elevator ride, with zero heard!
Stop jamming two word tasks onto one narrow stage!
Load one question onto the prefrontal cortex, your front planner.
Then step outside and leave the stage microphone quiet.
Your silent specialist rooms will return the missing answer.
Which proves consciousness is one shared stage, and quiet focus lets your brain shine.
